old_caption: The video showcases a close-up view of water, likely from a shallow pool or a calm body of water. The surface is rippled, creating a dynamic pattern of light and shadow. Sunlight filters through the water, casting intricate, wavy lines across the surface. These patterns shift subtly as the water moves, revealing the sandy bottom beneath. The colors are primarily shades of brown and beige, reflecting the natural environment. There are no visible animals or characters in the scene; the focus remains entirely on the interplay between light, water, and the underlying sand. The camera appears to be stationary, capturing the serene and tranquil movement of the water's surface.

caption: The video showcases a close, top-down view of a shallow water surface over a dark brownish substrate. A web-like network of bright yellowish-white sunlight caustics covers it entirely. The network continuously morphs as bright lines bend, stretch, merge and split, while luminous nodes drift across the frame. Bright patches expand, contract and shift position, yet the layout of dark cells enclosed by bright lines is retained. A small cluster of dark plant-like shapes hangs at the top edge, shifting horizontally and partly moving out of and back into view. No separate object, animal or person enters the water. The motion stays confined to the deforming light pattern and the sway of edge vegetation.

An internal editing cut is not evidence of physical motion connecting the views.

Check identification before physical interpretation: a reflection is not a separate actor;
a powder/smoke/liquid outline or shadow is not automatically the boundary of a solid object;
an apparent change caused by occlusion/viewpoint is not automatically material deformation.

camera tracking. A single visible texture/seam does not prove spin. Avoid unnecessary absolute
claims of stillness, no motion, no camera motion or 'exactly' synchronized changes.
Remove invented scene details and explanations, but keep clearly visible ongoing motion and
processes. Avoid deleting the real process merely because its cause lies outside the cropped window.
